findings.title: Negation inside the exception frame

findings.mechanism: Adhaban retains punishment; shadidan and the preceding active predicate supply harshness that makes the opposite ease branch perceptible.
findings.reader_payoff: Punishment can be sensed as withdrawal of ease while its ordinary penalty sense remains intact.
findings.containment: Sweetness is only a contrastive resonance; no sweet water, taste, or literal deprivation appears.

epistemic.reason: The candidate names the root polarity, while local severity activates it only by analogy.

findings.title: From fate to written basis
findings.claim: The coda pivots from the two active fate predicates to the written status of the decree.
findings.mechanism: After aw closes the alternatives, kana takes dhālika as subject and leads into the Book and final passive written predicate.
findings.reader_payoff: The final movement turns attention from what happens to how the disposition stands in the record.
findings.containment: The coda adds documentary status without cancelling or reinterpreting either outcome.

epistemic.reason: The clause boundary and predicate sequence support the structural pivot.

findings.title: Kana as established state
findings.claim: Kana presents the decree's written status as established, not merely as a past act of writing.
findings.mechanism: The perfect verb opens a predicate clause whose final passive participle describes the decree, giving the coda an existing-state force.
findings.reader_payoff: Writtenness is heard as settled status at the ayah's end.
findings.containment: This is a clause-level state reading and does not date when the decree was written.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology and candidate support identify the existential use and perfect aspect.

findings.title: Decree grounded in being
findings.claim: The existential force of kana makes the decree's writtenness feel established in being.
findings.mechanism: Kana carries occurrence and present-being pressure; dhālika specifies the decree and masṭuran its written state, so existence meets writtenness.
findings.reader_payoff: The recorded decree is perceived as settled reality rather than a newly proposed forecast.
findings.containment: This colors the existential clause; it does not make kana a separate noun or a metaphysical object.

epistemic.reason: The supplied root facet meets the local subject and predicate, while the result remains interpretive.

branch_activations.carrier: Kana carries existential and established-state predication.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Dhālika identifies the prior decree and masṭuran states its written condition.
branch_activations.activation: The being facet meets an already specified written decree.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Writtenness is presented as an established state of the decree.
branch_activations.boundary: The clause remains existential predication, not a new lexical object.

findings.title: Distance marks a fixed decree
findings.claim: Dhālika packages the preceding fate rule as a referent viewed at a distance, and the coda gives it written status.
findings.mechanism: The demonstrative gathers the alternatives as its subject; kana, the Book phrase, and masṭuran make that referent sound established.
findings.reader_payoff: The whole fate pair becomes one already settled object of the final statement.
findings.containment: Distance is deictic and interpretive, not literal spatial separation or proof that distance alone means permanence.

epistemic.reason: This is a local inference from distal reference meeting the written-state coda.

findings.title: Whole decree made one subject
findings.claim: The demonstrative compresses both fate alternatives into one referent for the written coda.
findings.mechanism: Dhālika follows both predicates and becomes kana's subject, allowing one inscription statement to cover their arrangement together.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees one decree being inscribed, not two disconnected outcomes.
findings.containment: The demonstrative gathers the preceding clause without choosing either fate or erasing their distinction.

epistemic.reason: The subject relation and backward referent are directly supported.

findings.title: Attachment reinforces writtenness
findings.claim: Whether fī al-kitāb attaches to the state clause or the final predicate, the Book location reinforces writtenness.
findings.mechanism: The prepositional phrase can modify kana's predication or masṭuran; either parse locates the decree in the Book and connects it to inscription.
findings.reader_payoff: The ambiguity yields two compatible contacts that both strengthen the documentary coda.
findings.containment: Both attachments remain possible; the finding does not adjudicate them or infer metaphysical depth.

epistemic.reason: The packet preserves an attachment ambiguity whose local readings converge without selecting one.

findings.title: Decree inside the Book
findings.claim: The final clause places the decree inside the definite Book or written register.
findings.mechanism: Fī supplies interior location and governs al-kitāb, while dhālika refers to the fate rule and masṭuran states its written condition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees containment in a named record rather than a loose association with writing.
findings.containment: Containment is the local spatial relation; no separate doctrine about metaphysical depth or surface is asserted.

epistemic.reason: Government and location are directly supplied.

findings.title: The known Book contains the decree
findings.claim: The definite Book is presented as a known written register that contains the fate rule.
findings.mechanism: Al-kitāb is definite and governed by fī; the preceding demonstrative refers to the rule placed there, giving the record institutional weight.
findings.reader_payoff: The decree appears in an identified register, not merely in writing somewhere.
findings.containment: The grammar supports a definite register; it does not specify a physical volume or outside institution.

epistemic.reason: Definiteness, government, and attachment are supplied by the focus evidence.

findings.title: Book mediates decree and writtenness
findings.claim: The Book stands between the packaged decree and its written predicate, sealing the coda as a contained record.
findings.mechanism: Dhālika gathers the alternatives; fī al-kitāb locates them in the register; masṭuran states their written condition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees active fate carried into contained documentary status at the end.
findings.containment: The structure adds fixity to the fate pair without turning the Book into a separate physical mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The relation is expressed by focus-local syntax and word order.

findings.title: Text, decree, and joined register

findings.mechanism: Aw separates two outcomes and dhālika gathers them; masṭuran and kana meet the root's written-fixing-of-judgment use.
findings.reader_payoff: The register feels ordered around one settled disposition rather than a loose list.
findings.containment: Joining is analogical and decree is root pressure; the lexical noun remains Book, not a verb meaning join or decree.

epistemic.reason: The local coda supplies triggers for the root contacts, but joining remains analogical.

findings.title: Civic fate schedule
findings.claim: The universal frame places each gathered settlement under two distinct fates before the Day of Resurrection, then presents the disposition as a fixed written ruling.
findings.mechanism: The negative-exception frame triggers the exhaustive civic class; paired active predicates distinguish extinction from penalty; qabla and al-qiyamah set their shared horizon; kitab and masṭuran return both outcomes as a written determination.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause reads as one locally bounded civic schedule rather than a bare prediction that every locality disappears.
findings.containment: This remains attributed to a legacy-unbound trace. Ordinary settlement, destruction, punishment, temporal, Book, and written senses remain; no date, itinerary, or surah-wide system is added.

epistemic.reason: Roots and word indices agree with QAC and focus branch records, but the interpretation remains attributed because the HFT reader identity is unbound.

findings.title: Settlement as a depleted reservoir
findings.claim: As an exploratory image, the gathered settlement can be felt as a reservoir whose severe punishment depletes and constricts it.
findings.mechanism: Qaryah's gathering/container branches are the carrier; halak's drought branch and ʿadhb's abstention/withholding branches are triggers; shadidan supplies constriction, turning civic ruin into ecological and alimentary depletion.
findings.reader_payoff: The second fate gains a possible mode of deprivation: a civic body can fail through what is withheld as well as through an external blow.
findings.containment: This legacy-unbound image is exploratory. The ayah names no water, rain, famine, or literal fasting; settlement, destruction, and severe punishment remain ordinary senses.

epistemic.reason: Roots, indices, and roles match focus occurrences, but the linked material-depletion image is multi-step and actual conditions are unstated.

branch_activations.boundary: The reservoir is an attributed analogy; stored water or food is not named.

findings.title: Written fate as ordered itinerary
findings.claim: As an exploratory spatial analogy, the written disposition can be pictured as an ordered itinerary of settlements, each assigned a terminal outcome before the final horizon.
findings.mechanism: Qaryah's route branch meets qabla's sequence; extinction supplies each stop's terminal encounter; the Book's joining facet links entries; masṭuran's cutting-line branch returns the sequence as marked inscription.
findings.reader_payoff: The written disposition can also be perceived as a sequence whose settlements each receive a terminal mark.
findings.containment: This is an attributed analogy only: the focus words still mean settlement, Book, and written status. No literal route, traversal, sword, or physical cut is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The exact local contacts return to focus, but the itinerary is a legacy-unbound outlier and the cut/route relation remains explicitly analogical.
